full_judgment:
Latifur Rahman, J: This appeal by the informant-appellant is against the judgment and order passed on 2.5.95 in Criminal Appeal No. 1157 of 1994 by a Division Bench of the High Court Division setting aside the judgment and order of conviction and sentence passed on 22.6.94 in Sessions Case No. 345 of 1992 by the Additional Sessions Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka convicting The accused-respondents under Section 302/34 of the Penal Code and sentencing each of them to suffer rigorous imprisonment for life and also to pay a fine of Tk. 10,000/- each in default, to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 2 years more. 

 2. The prosecution case is that on 13.8.91 at about 11-30 P.M. while Akber Sheith was coming to his house in a rickshaw accompanied by P.W.2 Sultan Ahmed, absconding accused Ataur, accused-respondents Ali Jan and Fazlu and others attacked Akber Sheith in front of Al Amin Transport, Armanitola within Dhaka City. Accused Ataur fired shot aiming at Akber Sheith and accused Ali Jan assaulted Akber Sheith in his shoulder with Chapati (Chinese) and accused Fazlu stabbed him on the head. The deceased was taken to Milford Hospital soon after the occurrence where he was declared dead. Further prosecution case is that the said Akber Sheith was a businessman in his locality. He took lease of a cattle market during Eid-Ul-Azha. On 25.6.91 he paid accused Ali Jan and others Tk. 25,000/- as remuneration for management of the said cattle market. The said Ali Jan took the money and started to abuse the mother of Akber stating that he has been given less money than he is entitled to. Akber Sheith having come to know of this behaviour of accused All Jan met him after 2/3 days at the market owned by Akber Sheith and slapped Ali Jan for abusing his mother Ali Jan became furious and left the place giving open threats that he would see Akber Sheith and thereafter this occurrence took place. 

 3. The defence case is that the accused persons are innocent who have been implicated in this case falsely leaving aside the real offenders. 

 (3) Motive being a very important and vital circumstance in this case, total non-consideration of the same has also materially affected the decision and the same has resulted in a miscarriage of justice resulting in an erroneous order of acquittal in the case. 

 (4) The medical evidence and the evidence of P.Ws. 1,3,5,6 and 14 have been discarded illegally which also materially and substantially corroborates the entire prosecution case as to the time, place and manner of occurrence and also of inflicting of injuries on the deceased. 

 5. In this case prosecution examined 23 witnesses, out of whom six were tendered and the defence did not examine any witness. 

 6. According to the First Information Report P.W.2 Sultan Ahmed appears to be the only eye witness of the occurrence. The further prosecution case is that P.W. 4 Abdul Aziz a night guard is also an eye witness to a part of the occurrence inasmuch as he saw accused-respondent No. 1 Ali Jan and respondent No. 2 Fazlu, Naim and Asad running away jumping the wall of Armanitola Field just after the firing sound came from the place of occurrence. P.W.2 Sultan Ahmed while deposing in court stated that Ataur fired a shot at deceased Akber Sheith accompanied by 2/3 persons, but he did not specifically name the accused-respondents or their role in the killing of Akber Sheith. P.W.2 was declared hostile after his examination-in-chief. He was cross-examined by the prosecution. P.W.2 Sultan Ahmed made a statement under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure within 5 days of the occurrence before P.W. 19 Md. Quddus, Magistrate, 1st Class wherein he stated in clear terms that absconding accused Ataur fired from his Kata rifle upon Akber Sheith and Ali Jan assaulted Akber Sheith in his neck with a Chapati and also spoke of the presence of Fazlu in his statement. He also stated in his statement that after Eid-Ul-Azha there was a quarrel over inadequacy of remuneration and deceased Akber Sheith was stabbed by Ali Jan. The trial Court considered the evidence of the recording Magistrate P. W.19 and found that Ext. 3 is not a product of coercion, inducement and threat. The trial court believed the statement as voluntary. The trial court was conscious that the statement, Ext. 3, being not a substantive evidence can be used to contradict or corroborate the maker thereof. The trial court found that P.W.2 Sultan Ahmed is not telling the truth in court after making a fatal departure from his earlier statement with a purpose to shield the accused respondents with a definite motive. 

 8. Mr. Serajul Huq, learned Advocate for the accused-respondents very frankly con-ceded that no question of admissibility of Ext. 3 is under challenge, but whether in the facts of the present case P.W.2 should be believed or not is the prime question. The trial court correctly enunciated the legal position and found that P.W.2 is not disclosing the whole truth in evidence in court and deliberately suppressing the truth to help the accused-respondents. Thus the learned Judges of the High Court Division erred in law in holding that the trial court treated the statement of P.W.2 Sultan as substantive evidence. The trial court correctly found that the attention of P.W.2 Sultan Ahmed was drawn to his earlier statement under Section-164 of the Code and held that this witness is not telling the truth to save the accused-respondents. 

 10. This material evidence of P.W.4 as to the presence of these two accused-respondents at the place of occurrence and their running away over the boundary wall of the field of Armanitola is a very strong circumstantial evidence. This aspect of the case had not at all been considered by the learned Judges of the High Court Division. This strong circumstance lends support to the presence of the accused-persons at night in the place of occurrence. Non-consideration of this material aspect has also resulted in a miscarriage of justice in the present case. A very strong piece of circumstantial evidence was totally left out of consideration by the learned Judges of the High Court Division. This is indeed a material omission of circumstantial evidence by the learned Judges of the High Court Division. 

 14. The circumstantial evidence as indicated in the testimony of P.W.4 Abdul Aziz who saw running away the accused-respondents soon after the occurrence, motive of this murder, the medical evidence on record and the testimony of P.Ws. 1,3,5 and 14 who are most natural and probable witnesses of the case have been left out of consideration without any cogent reason. 

 15. It was the duty of the learned Judges of the High Court Division to consider all these circumstances including the material fact that P.W.2 resided willfully from his previous statement to save the accused-respondents. In the facts and circumstances of the case, we are convinced that the order of acquittal has been passed upon a total disregard of the evidence on record and also on misinterpretation of evidence thereby resulting in a grave miscarriage of justice for which the order of acquittal needs to be set aside.
